[b]Saturday, 19th June 2027 | 9:23 AM Nestor Ocean Time |  Shuri Castle (首里城), Shurikinjocho District (首里金城町地区), Yamakagutsuchi (山カグツチ), Ryūkyū Province (琉球国), Iōjima Prefecture (硫黄島県), Anunshotō (暗雲諸島)[/b]

An announcement has been made by the [i]Kunaichō[/i] (宮内庁) in collaboration with the [i]Sunao Times[/i] (スナオタイムズ) informing the general public and international community of the passing of the 23[sup]rd[/sup] Tenshō of Anunshotō, Hamahiga Yamato (浜比嘉大和) yesterday morning before sunrise. Staff of the [i]Kunaichō[/i] found the Tenshō unresponsive in His bed at around 8:19 am on 18[sup]th[/sup] June during a routine check-on after heading to bed earlier the previous day. Doctors of the [i]Shodaigōzoku[/i] (初代豪族) stated that the Tenshō had passed away from a stroke that occurred during His sleep at roughly 3:28 am. The event was peaceful, and would have caused the Tenshō no distress or pain, allowing Him to enter [i]Takamagahara[/i] (高天原) alongside His forebearers. It was decided by the [i]Shodaigōzoku[/i] and the [i]Kunaichō[/i] to delay the announcement of the death of Tenshō Yamato as the [i]Kōtaison[/i] of Anunshotō, Michiyoshi (通良), was out of the country on a private family holiday with his wife and their three sons.

Born 10th August 1939 during the reign of His paternal grandfather, Tenshō Shirakawa (白川), as the first child of Tenshō Ishiō (石王) (at the time Tenshi Morosada (モロサダ)), His personal name was Jirō (次郎). When Tenshō Shirakawa died in 1945, Tenshi Jirō's father ascended the Erythrina Throne, and Jirō was proclaimed Tenshi of Anunshotō in 1954, making him the heir apparent at age 15. Tenshō Ishiō would pass away from cancer at 46 years of age on 25[sup]th[/sup] July 1956, and Jirō became the 23[sup]rd[/sup] Tenshō 16 days before His 17[sup]th[/sup] birthday. He became the 7[sup]th[/sup] youngest person to inherit the Erythrina Throne. He assumed the regal name of Yamato on 29[sup]th[/sup] July 1956.

Tenshō Yamato's reign of 70 years and 329 days is the longest of any Head of State since the unification of Anunshotō in 1429, surpassing that of Tenshō Meiji (明治; Personal name Hirohito (裕仁); Regal name Aoi (葵)) who reigned for 62 years and 245 days from 7 May 1817 - 7 January 1880. The reign of Tenshō Yamato marked further modernisation and greater economic growth, and as such His era, known as Natsukashii (懐かしい), is considered to be the most prosperous since the era of Tenshō Meiji. He became the first Tenshō to not only host foreign Head of States and Governments, but also the first to visit foreign countries. His status and image became strongly positive across the world and within Anunshotō. 

With the passing of Tenshō Yamato, He is to be succeeded by his eldest born son with [i]Kōgō[/i] (皇后) Dai, the Tenshi Osahito (治仁), who will become the 24[sup]th[/sup] Tenshō of Anunshotō since 1429. He is expected to assume a new regal name in the following week, as well as appoint his firstborn son, the current [i]Kōtaison[/i] of Anunshotō, Michiyoshi (通良) as the next Tenshi. Michiyoshi's firstborn son, Hijirō (聖郎), will in turn become the newest [i]Kōtaison[/i] at 11 years of age. Upon the coronation ceremony of Osahito, he will anoint Tenshō Yamato with a posthumous name which He will be known as.

Preparations are currently in motion for a State Funeral, and the [i]Sūmitsu-in[/i] (枢密院) has declared the rest of June to be a period of mourning.
[/spoiler]
